D Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com. h DILG OPINION No. 08 s.2b23 L NUEL R. LOPEZ Provincial Administrator Ilagan City, Province of Isabela Dear ANY. Lopez: This has reference to your letters dated November 12, 2021 and October II, 2022, requesting for the applicability of Section 133 vis-å-vis Section 141 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC). The matter before us stemmed from this Department's Legal Opinion No. 29, s.2019, pertinent portion of which reads: Nevertheless, for academic discussion and to avert the same controversy in the future, we are of the considered view that the subject ordinances are valid and reasonable as they are pursuant to Section 141 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code, viz: Section 141. Annual Fixed Tax For Every Delivery Truck or Van of Manufacturers or Producers, Wholesalers of, Dealers, or Retailers in, Certain Products. - (a) The province may levy an annual fixed tax for every truck, van or any vehicle used by manufacturers, producers, wholesalers, dealers or retailers in the delivery or distribution of distilled spirits, fermented liquors, soft drinks, cigars and cigarettes, and other products as may be determined by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, to sales outlets, consumers, whether directly or indirectly, within the province in an amount not exceeding Five hundred pesos (P500.00). The afore-quoted provision of the LGC should not be confused with Section 133(e) of the LGC, which provides that: "SECTION 133. Common Limitations on the Taxing Powers of Local Government Units. - Unless otherwise provided herein, the exercise of the taxing powers of provinces, cities, municipalities, and Barangays shall not extend to the levy of the following: xxx (e) Taxes, fee and charges and other impositions upon goods carried into or out of, or passing through, the territorial jurisdictions of local govemment units in the guise of charges for wharfage, tolls for bridges or otherwise, or other taxes, fees or charges in any form whatsoever upon such goods or merchandise. xxx" "Matlno, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Thus, what is prohibited is the collection of pass-through fees as contemplated in the Department's Memorandum Circular No. 2018- 133, dated 16 August 2018 and the annual fixed tax for every delivery truck or van as contemplated in Section 141 of the LGC. Hence, we are of the considered view that securing/purchasing of sticker is valid on the assumption that the stickers will be released/given as a proof/evidence that the said taxes/fees (Section 141 of the LGC) are already paid, aside from the official receipt that will be issued. (Emphasis ours) Hence, confusion arose relative to the applicability of Section 133 vis-å-vis Section 141 of the LGC. Foremost, in the highlighted portion of the subject opinion, specifically after the conjunction "and", it seems that the word "not" was inadvertently omitted. Upon careful evaluation of the tenor of the opinion, it appears that Sections 133 and 141 of the LGC were being compared/contradicted with each other. In fact, the subject matter of MC No. 2018-133 is the prohibition of imposing pass through fees as contemplated in Section 133 of the LGC. Accordingly, the highlighted portion is hereby amended: Thus, what is prohibited is the collection of pass-through fees as contemplated in the Department's Memorandum Circular No. 2018-133, dated 16 August 2018 and not the annual fixed tax for every delivery truck or van as contemplated in Section 141 of the LGC. This opinion serves as a clarification on Legal Opinion No. 29, series of 2019 dated June 24, 2019. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY A THORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . JUA OR R.
